Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we stay aligned on the performance/SLO qualification: 

Summary of requirements you shared:
- Latency targets: p90 end-to-end inference < 150ms for 512-token context (primary), p99 < 350ms (target)
- Throughput: sustained 800 requests/minute with bursts to 1,200/minute
- Concurrency: up to 80 simultaneous active streams
- Streaming: server-sent events (SSE) streaming with low inter-token latency (~<10ms preferred) and graceful reconnect behavior
- Determinism: need reproducible bench runs for A/B comparisons across model variants and quantization levels

What we will deliver by EOD tomorrow: 
1) A shared prompt set sample (small and full) — attached as edgefin_prompt_samples.zip.
2) Benchmark harness (v1) + reproducibility notes and run commands — linked in this thread.
3) Measurement definitions doc (p50/p90/p99, tokens/sec, tail latency, throughput measured at client vs. server) — attached as benchmark_results_template.xlsx

Open questions for you: 
- Are the latency numbers above end-to-end (client-perceived) or only server-side inference? We assumed end-to-end but want to confirm.
- For streaming, do you require ordered partial tokens (SSE) only, or would you accept chunked HTTP streaming?

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- You validate the prompt set (quick pass) — 1 business day
- We run internal harness on your sample (redwood-hosted) and share results — 2 business days after prompt sign-off
- Joint remote benchmark run (if you want to run in your environment) — schedule week of Jul 26

Attaching the initial files. Let me know if I missed anything.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency: the numbers I quoted on the call were client-perceived (end-to-end), which includes some client-side processing. For the benchmark, it would be helpful to see both server-only inference latency and end-to-end so we can isolate gaps.

2) Streaming: SSE is preferred. We need ordered partial tokens in real time. Chunked HTTP is acceptable only if token ordering and inter-token latency are comparable to SSE.

3) Concurrency: 80 concurrent streams is our peak functional requirement. For the benchmark, please include a run that simulates steady state at 80 concurrent streams plus a 30-minute burst run to 120 concurrency.

We reviewed the prompt samples briefly — looks representative. We'll confirm changes by tomorrow noon.

A couple asks for the harness: can you include warm-up runs and KV cache pre-seeding steps? We want the harness to make it easy to reproduce the exact warm state we discussed.

Thanks,
Alice
Head of ML Systems, EdgeFin
alice.chen@edgefin.com

Thanks Alice — that's very helpful. Answering your asks and adding more details below.

Server vs. end-to-end: we'll produce both. The harness will emit server-side inference timestamps (on the Redwood runtime side) as well as client-side receive timestamps so you can compute network and client-processing deltas.

Warm-up & KV pre-seeding: included. The harness will run a configurable warm-up phase (default 2 minutes) plus an optional KV cache pre-seed step. We'll provide a reproducible seed file you can use to prime KV entries before the measured run.

Planned benchmark run types (we'll provide scripts for each):
- Steady-state concurrency: 80 concurrent streams for 60 minutes with 5-minute sampling windows
- Burst run: ramp to 120 concurrent streams for 30 minutes, then return to steady-state
- Latency microbench: single-client repeatable requests (QPS sweep) to measure p50/p90/p99 at controlled token lengths (64/256/512)
- Streaming inter-token latency: measure median inter-token latency and 95th percentile inter-token gaps

Measurement definitions (short):
- p50/p90/p99: percentiles over request end-to-end latency measured at client receive time (ms)
- server_infer_pXX: percentiles measured inside the runtime from request arrive -> inference complete (ms)
- tokens_per_sec: average token emission rate during steady-state streaming (tokens/sec)
- error_rate: 4xx/5xx per 1000 requests
- successful_stream_completion: percent of streams that finish without reconnects

Reproducibility notes:
- Each run will include a 'run manifest' file containing: model name & checksum, model config (quantization), seed, harness commit SHA, hardware SKU, driver/cuda versions, and the exact prompt file used.
- We'll fix random seeds where possible and include the harness invocation command in the manifest.

Attachments included: benchmark_results_template.xlsx (definitions + expected sheet layout). Also uploaded the harness v1 to our private repo and a tarball (redwood_benchmark_harness_v1.tar.gz) — link below.

Link to harness & how to run (short):
- Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness/tree/v1
- Quick run (redwood-hosted, ephemeral env): 
  ./run_harness.sh --job edgefin-steady --concurrency 80 --duration 3600 --warmup 120 --seed 42 --output manifest_edgefin_20270720.json

I'll kick off an internal redwood run on the prompt sample you provided and share initial numbers by EOD tomorrow. If you want to run in your environment we can provision a joint session the week of Jul 26.

Cheers,
Marissa

Subject: Fwd: Performance SLO benchmark methodology follow-up

Looping in some implementation specifics from the runtime side — Alice, Bob, quick heads up on how we'll ensure measured numbers are meaningful and reproducible.

1) Server-side timestamps: we'll record these at these points: request_received, model_invoke_start, model_generate_first_token, model_generate_last_token, response_sent. These allow computing queue latencies, model initialization, and token generation windows.

2) Warm-up: critical to avoid cold-starts. We recommend: 3 sequential warm-up phases — a) model load & compile (one-time), b) small-batch warm-up (16 requests), c) steady warm-up at target concurrency for 2 minutes. Harness will optionally re-run (b) and (c) between model variant runs.

3) KV cache pre-seeding: we will provide a script to pre-seed KV with a fixed dataset and confirm hit rates before the measured window. Include hit_rate target in manifest.

4) Batching: harness will test with and without batching. For streaming runs we will run no-batching mode (continuous generation) and a small-batch mode (batch size 4) to show trade-offs.

5) Repro command snippet (example):

# reproducible run (redwood-hosted)
./run_harness.sh --job edgefin-steady --concurrency 80 --duration 3600 --warmup 180 --preseed kv_seed_20270720.json --model redwood-l2-8q --quantization 8bit --seed 42 --output results_edgefin_20270720.json

6) Manifest fields we will produce: model_name, model_sha256, quantization, hardware_sku, driver_versions, kernel_flags, harness_sha, prompt_set_sha, seed, run_start, run_end, attachments (prompt files).

A couple implementation notes to set expectations:
- Measured p99 end-to-end will often be dominated by network and client processing; we'll include both server-only and client-only breakdowns so you can interpret.
- For streaming inter-token latency we sample token gaps on both server and client to allow delta analysis.

I'll be available for a technical run-through tomorrow afternoon if you want to go line-by-line in the harness.

Vivek
